authoredPrompt: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for transcription position: drag along the DNA template, and the open bubble advances while the magenta mRNA strand grows 5' to 3' with each new complementary base, showing how the antisense strand directs RNA synthesis.
- Toggle between base-pairing views: switch among DNA-DNA pairs, DNA-RNA pairs, and sense-vs-mRNA comparison, and the relevant hydrogen bonds or matching letters highlight, making complementarity and the T-to-U substitution clear.
- Hover for individual bases: hover over any exposed DNA or mRNA base, and its paired partner and strand direction labels appear, showing which strand is read and which sequence matches the transcript.
authoredContext:
Following formation of the polymerase–promoter complex, several turns of the DNA double helix untwist, forming a bubble and exposing 14 or so base pairs of the two strands. Appropriate ribonucleotides then line up by hydrogen-bonding to their complementary bases on DNA, bond formation occurs in the 5′ → 3′ direction, the RNA polymerase moves along the DNA chain, and the growing RNA molecule unwinds from DNA (the figure). At any one time, about 12 base pairs of the growing RNA remain hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template.

Biosynthesis of RNA using a DNA segment as a template.

Several turns of deoxyribonucleic acid double helix unwind exposing bases of the two strands. Ribonucleotides line up such that hydrogen bonds form in 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

Unlike what happens in DNA replication, where both strands are copied, only one of the two DNA strands is transcribed into mRNA. The DNA strand that contains the gene is often called the sense strand, or coding strand, and the DNA strand that gets transcribed to give RNA is called the antisense strand, or noncoding strand. Because the sense strand and the antisense strand in DNA are complementary, and because the DNA antisense strand and the newly formed RNA strand are also complementary, the RNA molecule produced during transcription is a copy of the DNA sense strand. That is, the complement of the complement is the same as the original. The only difference is that the RNA molecule has a U everywhere that the DNA sense strand has a T.

demo_steps.title: Complete Transcript
demo_steps.narration: The transcription bubble is fully open, with the magenta mRNA strand synthesized against the cyan antisense template.

demo_steps.title: Growing the mRNA
demo_steps.narration: Drag the slider to see the mRNA grow 5' to 3'. New ribonucleotides pair sequentially with the template strand.

demo_steps.title: DNA-RNA Base Pairing
demo_steps.narration: The mRNA forms temporary base pairs with the antisense DNA. Notice that Adenine (A) on DNA pairs with Uracil (U) on RNA.

demo_steps.title: Comparing Sense and mRNA
demo_steps.narration: Comparing the mRNA directly to the top sense strand reveals they carry the identical sequence, except RNA uses U where DNA uses T.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Pure 2D layout (X spans -12.5 to +12.5, Y spans -5 to +5). Base spacing = 1 unit along X. Left paired region (X=-12 to -10): Sense (C A T), Antisense (G T A). Bubble region (X=-9 to +9): Sense (T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T), Antisense (A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A), mRNA (U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U). Right paired region (X=+10 to +12): Sense (G A C), Antisense (C T G). End region ribbon Y-coords: Sense = +2, Antisense = -2. Bubble region Y-coords: Sense = +4, Antisense = -4, mRNA = -2 (parallel to antisense). Bases point inward (Sense points down, Antisense points up, mRNA points down). Colors: Sense = #8B9DCC (blue-violet), Antisense = #4FC2F8 (cyan), mRNA = #ED64A6 (magenta). 5' and 3' labels: Sense (5' left, 3' right), Antisense (3' left, 5' right), mRNA (5' left, 3' right).
interactionPlan.notes: Animate the bubble parametrically: as transcriptionPos increases from 0 to 19, the separation of the DNA strands and the length of the mRNA strand should grow horizontally from X=-9 to X=-9+pos. Bases and stems outside the current bubble remain base-paired at Y=±2. Toggle highlights can be achieved by dimming non-relevant elements (opacity 0.2) and brightening the relevant strands/bonds (opacity 1.0).
